Ivy (AE): Quick heads-up — Atlas wants to replace VendorY's chat API with Redwood. They requested a 10-day evaluation window, pricing for ~1M tokens/mo, and their security team just sent an RFI. Asking for scope + owners.

Ravi (SE): I can run the POC. Need their representative request/response shapes and a sample corpus. They currently get responses as { \"response\": \"...\", \"norm\": true, \"trace\": {...} } — we stream token deltas which will look different to their client.

Lena (Eng): Behavioral note: VendorY applies reply-normalization + deterministic top-k sampling tuned to reduce hallucinations. We can tune temperature/top_p and add a post-process to mimic. We'll validate with semantic tests, not exact-string match.

Omar (SRE): RFI highlights: data residency, BYOK/KMS, retention windows, and static egress IPs. ops-bot flagged missing SOC2 artifact upload.

ops-bot: Auto-scan result — outstanding items: \"SOC2 report (REQ-A1)\", \"BYOK/KMS process (REQ-A2)\", \"IP allowlist range stability (REQ-A7)\". Link: /internal/security/atlas-rfi.

Ivy (AE): Customer success criteria they gave: 1) <=8% user-visible delta on critical prompts (measured by small NPS-style sample), 2) token billing variance <=3% (for invoicing parity), 3) streaming behavior parity for cancel/resume. Also they want a migration playbook for zero-downtime cutover.

Ravi (SE): Two migration paths: (A) adapter proxy that accepts VendorY payloads and rewrites -> Redwood API (fast; client unchanged). (B) direct client migration to Redwood SDK (cleaner; longer). Rough timelines: proxy ~48-72h to a working shim + smoke tests; client change ~2-3 weeks including regression. I'll draft both runbooks.

Lena (Eng): I'll run 250 representative threads from their sample set. Plan: run VendorY & Redwood candidate, compute per-utterance embedding cosine similarity, flag any pairs with similarity <0.92 for human review. Also capture token counts and response length distributions.

Ravi (SE): For token accounting differences we should normalize tokenizers — VendorY uses a custom bytepair variant. Diego (Solutions) usually normalizes to tiktoken for billing parity; will need their raw requests to do same.

Omar (SRE): Quick ballpark pricing (for commercial): hosted API ~ $30k/mo for 1M tokens (customer-facing invoice number; conservative). Dedicated reserved: baseline pool estimate $8k-$12k/mo depending on model family and throughput needs. These are placeholders — I'll produce a proper calc after they share QPS shape.

Ivy (AE): Thanks. They asked whether we can provide a short-lived dedicated pool for the POC with an SLA. Any blockers?

Omar (SRE): We can spin a temporary pool but legal needs to approve interim SLA. Also ops needs an IP egress block to hand to the customer for allowlisting. I'll assemble the IPs and expected window.

Lena (Eng): Small technical note: VendorY strips leading/trailing whitespace and enforces a stop-token sequence. We'll add a post-process transformer in the shim to mimic that behavior to reduce surface diffs.

Ravi (SE): Example shim rewrite (draft):
```
POST /vendorY/chat
Host: proxy.atlas
{
  "conversation_id": "abc",
  "messages": [ {"role":"user","text":"Hello"} ]
}
# proxy rewrites -> curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
#   -d '{"input":"...","stream":true}' and returns VendorY-shaped envelope
```
(we return the same outer envelope and map streaming chunks into VendorY's single-response format for their client)

Ivy (AE): They also asked for an example reconciliation report for billing. Can we commit to producing a sample token-reconciliation CSV after the run (per-utterance: vendor_tokens, redwood_tokens, pct_delta)?

Lena (Eng): Yes — eval job will emit CSV with fields: id, vendor_tokens, redwood_tokens, cosine_sim, status. We'll also include a short diff excerpt for low-sim cases.

Omar (SRE): Security follow-ups: we can offer KMS BYOK for the POC but need ops checklist completed. Retention defaults are 30 days unless they sign for extended logs. Are they requesting longer?

Ivy (AE): Their security lead asked for 365-day audit log retention for compliance. That might be an add-on. Put it on the checklist.

Ravi (SE): OK action items and owners:
- Ivy: confirm kickoff date + get sample payloads and the NPS-like prompt set from Atlas
- Lena: run 250-thread comparison, produce CSV and flagged cases (ETA 48h after samples)
- Omar: sizing calc + IP egress block + legal intro for SLA (ETA 24h)
- Ravi: prototype proxy shim and doc timelines (ETA 48h prototype)
- ops-bot: re-run RFI scan after SOC2 artifact upload

Ivy (AE): I'll schedule kickoff for Tue 09:00 PT and upload Atlas samples when I have them. Agree on the 3 success criteria and will negotiate the retention term.

ops-bot: Reminder queued — please attach SOC2 report to /internal/security/atlas-rfi to clear REQ-A1.

Lena (Eng): I'll also log a small human-review sheet for product to triage differences. Will post link here when ready.

Ravi (SE): If anyone sees unexpected blocker (esp. legal or KMS provisioning) ping me and I'll escalate.

Ivy (AE): Thanks all — I'll share updates after kickoff confirm. :thumbsup:
